key: A small kirana shop is losing customers
name: ch20_kirana_price_board
alt: A kirana owner puts up a price-comparison board by his door with the supermarket receipt pinned beside it, and customers stop to read it.
scene: A street-level view of the front of a small Indian kirana shop on a residential lane, morning. The shop has a rolled-up shutter, shelves of packets and sacks of rice and sugar at the front. In the CENTRE, beside the door, stands a large whiteboard on an easel with two neat columns of prices for everyday items, little icons of an oil bottle, milk packet, sugar, atta and soap at the left of each row; the left column is ticked in green next to each lower price. At the top of the board a bold label reads "PRICE CHECK". Pinned to the right edge of the board is a long white supermarket receipt curling slightly, and a small tag on the board reads "Monday". In the shop door on the RIGHT, the owner, a man in his forties in a blue checked shirt with a pencil behind his ear, stands quietly with his arms folded and a small confident smile, not arguing with anyone. On the LEFT, three customers have stopped to read the board: a woman in a sari with a cloth shopping bag leaning closer, an older man with a walking stick pointing at one row, and a college student in a red T-shirt with a backpack, mouth open in surprise. In the far background, faint, a big boxy supermarket building. Bright morning light, quiet triumphant mood.

key: Two pressure-cooker sellers at a Diwali
name: ch20_pressure_cooker_mela
alt: Two pressure-cooker stalls at a Diwali fair: one seller holds up a leaflet to an empty space, the other cooks rajma on a burner with the whistle blowing and a queue forming.
scene: A wide view of two side-by-side stalls at an evening Diwali mela, strings of lamps and paper lanterns overhead and diyas along the front of each stall. LEFT stall: a seller in a striped shirt stands behind a table of shiny boxed pressure cookers, holding up a printed leaflet with tiny bullet lines on it; nobody stands in front of his stall except one passer-by walking past without looking. Above the left stall a bold label reads "LEAFLET". RIGHT stall: a seller in an orange kurta and apron stands at a gas burner on which a pressure cooker is cooking; a white puff of steam shoots up from the whistle with little sound lines, and a steel pot of red-brown rajma sits beside it. He is holding out a small spoon of rajma to the first person in a queue: a girl in a festive lehenga, behind her a man in a kurta, a grandmother and a young couple, all leaning forward, one already tasting and smiling. Above the right stall a bold label reads "DEMO". A thin vertical divider separates the two stalls. Warm festive light and a playful mood; the difference in crowd tells the story at a glance.

key: A water-purifier salesman in a Chennai
name: ch20_water_tester_readings
alt: A water-purifier salesman tests two glasses in a family kitchen: the tap water glass shows 480 and the purifier glass shows 40, while the family stares at the screen.
scene: A bright kitchen in a Chennai apartment, with a steel sink, a tap, a gas stove and a calendar on the tiled wall. In the CENTRE on the kitchen counter stand two clear glasses of water side by side, each with a small pen-shaped digital tester dipped into it showing a little screen. The LEFT glass, slightly cloudy, sits under the tap; its tester screen shows a large red number "480", and above it a bold label reads "TAP". The RIGHT glass, crystal clear, sits next to a compact white wall-mounted purifier demo unit; its tester screen shows a green number "40", and above it a bold label reads "FILTER". To the far RIGHT the salesman, a young man in a light blue uniform shirt with a toolkit bag, simply points at the two readings without speaking, eyebrows raised. On the LEFT, the family looks on: a mother in a cotton saree holding a steel tumbler she had been about to drink from, now frozen halfway, a father in a vest and lungi leaning in with his hand on his chin, and a schoolboy pointing at the red 480. Clear morning light, a mood of sudden personal realisation.

name: ch20_milk_bowling_league
alt: A child knocks down plastic-bottle pins in a hallway after finishing a glass of milk, while his father commentates dramatically and his mother cheers.
scene: A lively hallway inside an Indian flat in the evening, with a long tiled floor, a shoe rack, a framed family photo and a window showing a dark blue sky with a moon. In the foreground on the LEFT, an empty steel glass with a white milk ring sits on a small stool, next to a little chart of ticks pinned on the wall. The seven-year-old boy, in a striped T-shirt and shorts, has just rolled a soft ball down the hallway; he leans forward on one leg with arms up in excitement, a milk moustache on his upper lip. On the RIGHT end of the hallway, six plastic water-bottle pins arranged in a triangle are flying apart in all directions with little motion lines. Above the flying pins a bold label reads "STRIKE". In the CENTRE background, the father, in a kurta and spectacles, crouches like a sports commentator holding a steel ladle as a pretend microphone, mouth wide open in a shout, one fist pumping. Beside him the mother, in a nightie with a dupatta over her shoulder, claps with a satisfied grin. Warm indoor lamplight, joyful, playful mood; the milk has become the ticket to the game.

key: A flat owner in Pune has been asking the
name: ch20_tick_box_note
alt: A flat owner drops a printed tick-box note with a pen clipped on into the building secretary's letterbox, and the next morning it comes back ticked.
scene: A stairwell in a Pune apartment building with a row of metal letterboxes on the wall and a window showing the terrace above, where a pipe drips water into a bucket with small blue drops. In the CENTRE LEFT, the flat owner, a woman in her late thirties in a kurta and jeans with her hair in a bun, slides a neat printed white note into one of the letterboxes. A large inset card in the CENTRE shows the note close up: three square check boxes in a row with short words beside them, "SAT", "SUN", "MON", and a blank line for a time, with a blue pen clipped to the top edge. Above the card a bold label reads "TICK A DAY". On the RIGHT, a small inset bubble shows the next morning: the same note on her doormat beside a newspaper and a milk packet, with the "SUN" box firmly ticked in blue and a small green tick badge, and a faint sunrise in the window. In the far background on the stairs, the busy building secretary, a man with a stack of files and a phone at his ear, is hurrying upward. Soft daylight, neat and practical mood.

key: A young engineer goes to a society meeting
name: ch20_solar_slide_argument
alt: At a society meeting, a young engineer and a retired uncle argue over a datasheet on the projector while the clock runs forty minutes and the vote box stays empty.
scene: An interior view of a housing society community hall in the evening, rows of plastic chairs, a ceiling fan and a white projector screen at the front. On the projector screen a slide shows a dense chart and a small page counter "1/30", with a tiny solar panel icon. Standing beside the screen on the LEFT, the young engineer, a woman in her late twenties in a teal kurta with a laptop and a clicker, points sharply at a datasheet she has pulled up, her face tense. In the front row on the RIGHT, a retired uncle with white hair, spectacles and a sweater vest is half-standing, wagging a finger at the screen and arguing. Between them crossed jagged lines show the back-and-forth argument. Behind them, other residents slump in their chairs: one yawning, one looking at a phone, one dozing. On the wall, a clock shows forty minutes passing with a shaded arc. On a small side table near the front sits a clear ballot box, completely empty, and above it a bold label reads "NO VOTE". A whiteboard behind lists agenda lines, with the first line ticked and an arrow pointing to the next. Flat fluorescent light, tired, frustrated mood: she wins the argument and loses the decision.

key: A sales rep for a spice brand meets the
name: ch20_garam_masala_packets
alt: A spice sales rep lays out twelve rival masala packets with sticky notes on a buyer's desk, and the buyer opens and sniffs them while the clock runs past lunch.
scene: A view of a supermarket chain purchase office: a wide desk, a window with a city view, and a wall clock showing a quarter past one with a small lunch plate icon beside it. Across the desk in a neat grid of three rows lie twelve small spice packets in different bright colours, each with a yellow sticky note stuck on top showing a tiny rupee sign, a small face or a circular arrow. Above the grid a bold label reads "12 RIVALS". On the LEFT, the sales rep, a man in his thirties in a white shirt and a lanyard, stands relaxed with one open hand gesturing to the packets; on the floor beside him a closed laptop bag shows he no longer needs his spreadsheet. On the RIGHT, the purchase head, a woman in her forties in a smart blazer over a kurta with reading glasses pushed up, has opened one packet and holds it close to her nose with her eyes closed, little aroma swirls rising; her other hand already reaches for the next packet. A small inset in the top LEFT corner shows the previous meeting: the same two people frowning across a laptop with a bar chart and a red cross. Bright midday light, engaged, curious mood.
